rv.q: So, a well-put together, beautifully choreographed production but one with a frustrating emotional vacuum at its centre.
We gain a new angle but lose something at the same time.
For all his charisma, the evening winds up fast-paced but fatally unmoving.
But despite the production’s atmospheric aesthetics, its lack of focus means it never grips as it should.
So we’re left with a fitful evening that lurches from one lush tableau to another.
It’s a compelling reading of Shakespeare’s play, even if it loses its way when its deathtoll climbs.
Hastie has provided a handsome, clear-sighted production.
At the National Theatre, it feels below par.
Challenging, entertaining, and compelling, it takes one of the most well-known plays in the English language and shows us something new.
